A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Adaptive ε-PAL and retain matching algorithms, assumptions, and sample-complexity results despite the changed title. All 57 pages of v2 and 41 pages of v3, including their proof appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original synthetic GP experiments measuring accuracy, coverage, hypervolume, mean-squared error, and runtime across five setups.

after.justification: Section 7 reports original GP simulations, including accuracy/coverage confidence intervals, mean-squared errors, runtimes, and termination evaluation counts.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the matched algorithm sections retain the same GP inference, confidence regions, discarding, covering, refinement, and termination rules. The practical maximum-depth truncation variant also appears in both versions.

E1.justification: Evaluation coverage contracts from five synthetic setups to the one-dimensional, two-objective squared-exponential setup. The Matérn-5/2 and two-dimensional input scenarios in v2 Section 6.3.2 disappear and are not restored in v3's appendices.

E2.justification: The retained comparison evaluates the same PESMO, ParEGO, and USeMO baselines. V3 newly describes unsuccessful attempts to run original ε-PAL, but explicitly excludes it from the reported comparisons; v2 also provides no completed ε-PAL comparison.

E3.justification: V3 reports a design using 10 GP functions with five runs each, whereas v2's Simulation I presents a single sampled-function comparison. Hypervolume evaluation is removed. The rewritten metric descriptions also introduce ε-domination checks alongside retained 2ε criteria, leaving their operational relationship unclear. Kernel parameters, depth settings, and baseline budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 retains the maximum-depth and evaluation-threshold comparisons but removes substantial diagnostic evidence: predicted-front error visualizations, the target-ε sensitivity examples at 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 in Figure 9, and the hypervolume-versus-evaluations trajectories in Figure 11.

E5.justification: V2 already reports ten-run averages with unspecified error bars in Figure 11, while Simulation I uses point estimates. V3 removes those curves and explicitly reports 99% confidence intervals in Table 2, together with 10 function draws and five differently seeded runs per function. This revises the reported replication and uncertainty scheme without establishing an increase in matched runs.

E6.justification: V3 replaces the retained comparison's point results with reported aggregates: target-threshold accuracy/coverage means are 98%, 99%, and 99% for depths 24, 10, and 9, versus v2's reported 100% each. It adds approximate termination counts of 50, 40, and 35 evaluations and removes the other scenarios' results. These are revised summaries under a different reported aggregation design; runtime entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The main assumptions, theorem, and proofs are retained; v2's linear-information-gain example becomes Proposition 1 with its proof in Appendix B. However, v3 Section 7.1 adds mathematical characterizations equating ε-domination checks with 2ε conditions. Those equivalences do not hold under the unchanged Definition 1.

C1.justification: The adaptive-discretization contribution and both sample-complexity claims remain. V3 replaces v2's introduction claim of outperforming ε-PAL in accuracy and sample complexity on several benchmark datasets with an accuracy claim against competitors on synthetic multi-objective functions.

C2.justification: V3 adds the limitation that ε-PAL comparisons could not be completed. It explains departures from 100% performance through probabilistic guarantees and front discretization, and gives a more qualified interpretation of PESMO and ParEGO. The depth/runtime tradeoff and sparse-output explanation for USeMO largely remain.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies the experimental domain [0,1], observation-noise standard deviation 0.01, and USeMO's Tchebycheff aggregation. These are additional disclosures rather than established implementation changes. It removes the Adaptive ε-PAL implementation link supplied in v2, while retaining baseline-code links.

R1.justification: V3 substantially revises positioning through newer Pareto-learning, bandit, and joint-entropy-search literature, including Lin et al. (2022), Tu et al. (2022), and Kone et al. (2023), and expanded contrasts with ε-PAL. It also reverses the description of prior hypervolume methods' guarantees: v2 credits Daulton et al. (2020) with convergence guarantees, whereas v3 characterizes these methods as lacking them.

P1.justification: The title, author list, and affiliations change. Related work becomes a separate section with three subsections, and the experimental narrative is extensively rewritten. References move before the appendices, an appendix contents list is added, and the information-gain example moves out of the main text.

P2.justification: V2's experimental Figures 4–11 disappear. Some Simulation I information is consolidated into v3 Tables 2–3, while separate accuracy/coverage plots, Pareto-front visualizations, and multi-scenario plots are removed. Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix, Figures 1–3 remain, and the document adopts a substantially denser layout.

improvement.justification: V3 makes uncertainty reporting more explicit and aligns empirical claims with the reported baselines. These gains coexist with lost Matérn/two-dimensional validation and removal of the implementation link. New metric-characterization ambiguities and the results text's 99% claim versus Table 2's 98% for depth 24 also weaken clarity. The benefits and harms do not support a reliable overall quality direction.
